## Fix-plan detail (moved out of the description to keep it under the P4 admission limit)

**Three init gates, precisely.** `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` (a `.git`-presence check on
the low-level append path); `_seam.append_event` at `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:555` (the
AUTHORITATIVE write-command gate, requires `.env-id`; bug roar-nurse-stomp / ab61; pinned by
`tests/unit/test_store_copy_needs_env_id.py`); and the read chokepoint `_reads._tracker`. The one
message string is emitted from ~14 sites enforcing two different preconditions, so read and write
do NOT fully agree by design.

**Why reads deliberately do NOT require `.env-id`.** `.env-id` is git-ignored LOCAL provenance
state, absent immediately after a valid clone. Verified in-session: a store with `.git` + a
resolvable HEAD but no `.env-id` reads its tickets fine, while a write is correctly rejected by
the `_seam` `.env-id` gate. So a just-cloned store MUST stay readable; only writes require the
provenance stamp. The fix therefore closes the `.git`/HEAD read/write disagreement (broken /
mid-clone store readable-as-empty) and intentionally leaves the `.env-id` asymmetry alone.

**Write-gate behavior change + safety (addresses plan-review BLOCK rev2).** Sharing the `.git`+HEAD
predicate means `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` now also rejects a `.git`-present-but-HEAD-
unresolvable (mid-clone) store. Proven safe for the init/first-write path: instrumenting the call
showed `_ensure_initialized` is invoked exactly once across `init_repo` + first `create_ticket`,
and at that call HEAD already resolves -- init creates the store's initial commits through
`init_core`, not through the guarded append path. The full write suite is re-run at GREEN to
confirm no other write path appends into an unborn-HEAD store.

**Pre-mortem (how could this fail?).** (1) init writes before the first commit -> RULED OUT
(single `_ensure_initialized` call, HEAD resolves). (2) another write path appends to an
unborn-HEAD store -> guarded by re-running the full write suite at GREEN. (3) `git` binary absent
-> the predicate's `subprocess.run` uses `check=False`; a nonzero rc means "HEAD not resolvable"
(not usable), while an OSError (git missing) is a distinct environment failure that propagates
rather than masquerading as `store_uninitialized`; covered by a test. (4) perf: `git rev-parse`
per read is negligible -- the read path ALREADY spawns git (throttled `git fetch`/reconverge via
`_fresh`), so no new process class. (5) walk-up false positive -> the explicit `.git`-exists check
precedes the HEAD probe.

**Prior art.** git invoked via `git -C tracker rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, matching the existing
`footprint._git` read-probe pattern; the heavier `gitutil.run_git` is deliberately not reused so
the read chokepoint does not import the write-core lock machinery and `_reads` stays out of the
import SCC.
